requirement:
For every non-distributed requirement's structural check under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.structural_review`, every direct implementation
reference or `:impl:` anchor outside a declaration MUST contribute its source
selection to the initial mandatory inputs under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`, including when the requirement
also has incoming `{test}` references or `:test:` anchors. An in-source reference selects
its enclosing outline node, or the whole file when it has no language outline;
an anchor selects its named file or node. Source access, exclusions, errors,
and deduplication follow the existing mandatory-input rules. Refining
declarations continue to contribute their complete text. Implementation
helpers are requested when needed, rather than supplied recursively.
rationale:
**Verdict:** the only gap is acknowledged by an open `{fixme}`. I did not read the implementation. I judged only the two supplied tests against the requirement text.

**Gap: mixed requirements (acknowledged).**
- `requirements.authoring.structural_inputs` says every direct `{impl}` reference or `:impl:` anchor MUST contribute its source to the initial mandatory inputs. It adds "including when the requirement also has incoming `{test}` references or `:test:` anchors".
- In `src/authoring/mod.rs#mod[tests]/fn[structural_roots_select_inputs_and_version_the_reference_digest]`, the mixed case adds a `{test}` reference next to the `{impl}` reference and anchor. It then asserts `!tested.structural` and that no input has `item == "fn[api]"`. That is the opposite of the requirement for mixed requirements.
- The same opposite expectation appears where a `:test:` anchor replaces the `:impl:` anchor. That case only asserts `!structural`, which is correct for it, since no `{impl}` edge remains.
- The `{fixme}` on `src/authoring/inputs.rs#impl[AssessmentSources]/fn[prepare_with_context]` describes exactly this gap. Mixed requirements omit implementation roots, and the input tests assert that compromise instead of the full contract. Its issue, nikomatsakis/habeas-codicem#51, is open, so the gap is acknowledged.

**Other obligations: covered by the two tests.**
- **Anchor contributes its selection.** `:impl: src/lib.rs#fn[api]` yields an input with `item == "fn[api]"`. Its text contains `helper();` but not `fn helper`, which also shows helpers are not supplied recursively.
- **In-source reference selects its enclosing node.** With the anchor removed, `unanchored.mandatory_inputs()` equals the earlier inputs.
- **Whole file without an outline.** `src/details.txt` is included with `item == ""` and its full text.
- **Deduplication.** The anchor and the in-source reference give exactly one `src/lib.rs` root.
- **Refining declarations contribute complete text.** The `requirements.refined` input contains both paragraphs, "Complete refinement." and "Second paragraph.".
- **Non-distributed only.** Examples, distributed requirements (with a `{sites}` block) and requirements whose only reference sits in a refining declaration do not become structural. A plain-text-only implementation is also not structural.
- **Disallow.** `habeas.toml` with `disallow=['src/lib.rs']` aborts, and the error contains "disallowed".
- **Missing or unresolvable node.** `fn[missing]` gives an error containing "missing".
- **Default exclusion of generated evidence.** `evidence/generated.rs` is omitted by default. An explicit `allow` includes it. An omitted generated `:test:` edge does not override a real implementation. An allowed one does.
- **Staleness.** Structural sources are recorded as dependencies. The reference set changes, and an input change is flagged as a stale review.

**Conclusion.** The remaining mixed-input gap is covered by the open `{fixme}` for nikomatsakis/habeas-codicem#51.

text: :::{req} structural_inputs
For every non-distributed requirement's structural check under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.structural_review`, every direct implementation
reference or `:impl:` anchor outside a declaration MUST contribute its source
selection to the initial mandatory inputs under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`, including when the requirement
also has incoming `{test}` references or `:test:` anchors. An in-source reference selects
its enclosing outline node, or the whole file when it has no language outline;
an anchor selects its named file or node. Source access, exclusions, errors,
and deduplication follow the existing mandatory-input rules. Refining
declarations continue to contribute their complete text. Implementation
helpers are requested when needed, rather than supplied recursively.
:::{req} structural_review
For every non-distributed requirement, the assessment MUST identify its stated
structural properties, including signatures, type and field relationships,
ownership, and required delegation through interfaces. With incoming `{impl}`
references or `:impl:` anchors, it MUST check that the supplied implementation
roots support every such property under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.structural_prompt`. Without those edges, it MUST
establish that the requirement has no structural properties needing
implementation evidence; an unmet structural obligation MUST be a gap.
Incoming `{test}` references or `:test:` anchors MUST NOT skip this check.
References and anchors are those considered under
{cite}`requirements.references.discovery` and the existing source-access
policy; omitted generated evidence MUST NOT count as an edge. Obligations
delegated to refining declarations follow
{cite}`requirements.ci.review_criteria`. Examples, distributed requirements,
citation reviews, and site reviews retain their own assessment tasks.
:::{req} mandatory_inputs
The harness MUST construct each assessment's mandatory input set by combining
the contributions specified by the requirements applicable to that subject and
its inputs. A requirement that contributes inputs MUST cite this requirement and
define which sources it contributes and when. The harness MUST include every
applicable contribution, deduplicate identical selections, and report
unresolvable mandatory inputs before inference. The complete set MUST be supplied
in the initial model request.
Generated output under project-root `evidence/`, including symlink aliases, MUST
be omitted from mandatory inputs when the default exclusion applies. An explicit
workspace allow MUST permit those selections; an explicit disallow MUST abort
under {cite}`requirements.authoring.read_denial.mandatory`.
